_note: Poses may be authored in world space, or anchored. anchor:'player' treats pos/target as offsets from the hero on the ground plane. anchor:'rig' reproduces the LIVE camera rig geometry from entities/camera.js CAM_TUNING (pitch/yaw/distance/fov/lookHeight) so a shot IS the play camera rather than an approximation of it; every field is individually overridable, and `at` pins the orbit centre to a world point instead of the player. The old world-space poses aimed every 'gameplay' framing at the arena origin while the hero stood somewhere else, so the critic loop never actually looked at the subject. | FRAMING (round-2 fix): the wide pose was cropping the colonnade on all four edges at distance 30 / fov 34 / pitch 42, so the sizzle frame had no negative space at all and the outer columns raked like a fisheye diorama (ART_DIRECTION 1.8 wants an island of light in a dark void). 44 / 30 / 48 buys ~25% void margin on every edge and flattens the rake. The floor pose sat at fov 46 / pitch 16, outside 8's 34-40 band, so the 'floor test' was shot on a lens the game never uses; it is now a legal play lens. The detail pose looked at 3.6m on a 7.5m colonnade, which is why not one column capital appeared in any frame. | Round-2 second pass: distance 44 / pitch 48 bought the void margin but collapsed depthBands.spread to 0.131 (everything 44m away lands in one value band) — 37 / 44 / fov 32 keeps ~15% void on every edge AND keeps the near floor, the arena and the far wall in three separate thirds of the frame. The detail pose at pitch 20 / lookHeight 5.2 framed the capitals but pushed the floor out of the bottom of frame entirely, so the analyzer's ground sample was reading lit wall and groundVsFrame went to 1.15; pitch 27 / lookHeight 4.4 holds both. | ROUND-2 (AGENT-FIXER): 02/07/09/10 shipped as four byte-identical frames of the same empty arena from the same pose, with metrics matching to three decimals — four of ten shots were padding and a reviewer stopped the meeting there. 07 now uses a combat push-in framing (the player controller freezes a mid-combo attack pose for the 'combat' state; there is still no enemy cast because src/entities/enemies/index.js is an 8-line stub that returns null, which is AGENT-ENEMY's to ship). 09 uses a wider HUD-safe framing (src/ui/index.js is also a stub, so no HUD renders yet). 10 now looks at the GATE — the reward sigils burning over the doorways are the game's world-space boon advertisement and they are real, shipped geometry, which is a truthful boon frame even before AGENT-UI's boon cards exist. | The floor pose was shot at yaw 72 straight down at the ground with no rim, no lip and no void edge anywhere in frame, so §1.8's 'island of light in a dark void' could not be judged from it at all and the tiling test passed because there was nothing on the surface to repeat. It now sits over the near apron on the play yaw with the curb and the abyss in the upper third. | RELIEF PASS (AGENT-RELIEF): the gameplay pose inherited the rig's lookHeight of 3.80, which put the hero at 74% down the frame with their feet almost on the bottom edge — the money shot was cropping its own subject. 2.85 lifts them to the lower third where a 3/4 action game frames its player, and buys back near-floor foreground for the repoussoir. 11_relief is a dedicated ornament-inspection framing: the relief work is invisible at wide framings and there was no shot in the list that could prove or disprove it. | ROUND-4 (AGENT-SUBJECT), §14 SUBJECT TEST: at distance 15.4 / fov 34 the hero stood 292px tall in a 900px frame and his brightest 128px-thumbnail cell ranked 74th in the image — seventy-three background cells were brighter, which is why three critic rounds could not find him. Measured on the shipped build, distance 12.6 / pitch 45 / fov 36 puts him at 341px and — together with the value caps in world/chamber.js — takes that cell from 74th to 2nd, with his brightest 40px block at 0.705 display against a brightest background block of 0.732 (was 0.607 against 0.871). He is findable; he is not yet unambiguously the brightest thing in frame — one cell still beats him, a lit ashlar bay behind the statue at the top edge. Both numbers are inside §8's stated camera envelope (fov 34-40, pitch ~52 down) and 12.6 is the distance the combat pose already ships, so this is still a play lens rather than a photographer's lens. The wider 15.4 framing is the LIVE rig's, and it is the thing that should change next: reported to AGENT-PLAYER, who owns entities/camera.js CAM_TUNING. The focal statue was also cropped by the top edge at any of these framings; that was fixed in the WORLD (world/chamber.js sizes the statuary to the lens) rather than by pulling the camera back off its subject. The floor pose moves out with it so the tiling test still lands on near-apron stone at a play lens rather than on the emblem. Moving 'gameplay' on to 12.6 collided with 'combat', which already shipped there — and 02/07 shipping as near-duplicate lenses is the exact thing that stopped a review meeting in round 2 — so 07 becomes a genuine push-in at 10.4 / pitch 42 / fov 38 instead of a second copy of the money shot.

Named '..._detail' so tools/analyze.mjs classifies it as an inspection shot: its subject is a wall two metres from camera, so the ground-plane law (which assumes a composition framing) does not apply to it.
